sections.title: Player text
sections.body: The Custodian leads you out of the treehouse, out of the forest itself, to look down on the green expanse from above. Twisting stone spires break through the treeline, each with a flame flickering in its tower like a beacon. "There's a relay out west," she says, "maybe a few hours. You might have felt it on the way in: its light was weaker than it should be. I think something's wrong with its Keeper, and I fear what happens if that fire goes out." She studies the horizon. "When you're ready, come back. I'll give you my map, so you can make it there safe. It's good to have heroes in the preserve again."

Gmnotes: The Relay is seen and described, not entered. If epilogue_tone is pyrrhic or tragic, the hook feels like unfinished business rather than excitement.
Gmscript: Say: "One more thing on the horizon. Not tonight unless you want it tonight: a fire going dim, a Keeper in trouble, and a map waiting if you ever come back."

Gmchecklist: Deliver official Relay hook player-facing. Offer the map as a future door, not a forced next scene. Drop 0-4 hidden hints only if earned and the players bite. Let players say the conclusion; do not lecture. Set relay_hook_accepted, hidden_hook_discovered, and sequel_direction. End open-ended. No combat, no countdown, no next act transition.

Gmprivate: Hidden thesis: the corporation manufactures the peril it profits from protecting against. The official hook and hidden hook point to the same future destination, but the table only gets the hidden conclusion if they articulate it. Hint ladder: convenient Relay failure; the Custodian almost saying safety is not made from nothing; Bramble truth if learned; staged attack/defensive monster/trademarked havens/assets pattern if they connect it. Hold the soul-economy as a seed. Do not explain the mechanism.
Playertakeaway: You can rest easy tonight, and if you want, a door west is open.
Storytakeaway: The night's won, but a distant light is failing and the party may be the kind of people who answer.

Storyscope: Perceived antagonist: the forest. True antagonist: the corporate lie about the forest. The players never confront it directly. They are meant to feel it by the end. Every act offers at least one guaranteed and one earned hint that the danger is manufactured and the forest is not the enemy. The ritual completes, Hush is safe, and the Custodian thanks them. The win is real. KEEP GUARANTEED A Grail/Kazrak incident report thanks them for "neutralizing forest hazards" and supporting continued Protection Coverage. ADD GUARANTEED If pushed, the Custodian admits the "hazards" were not always here, then looks away. ADD EARNED Presence Hard 20 A nearby Relay Spire beacon burns weakly, pointing to the larger thread. KEEP GUARANTEED A nearby Relay Spire beacon burns weakly, pointing to the larger thread. KEEP GUARANTEED Presence Hard 20: draw out the Custodian's slip.
